requirement: `message` sets the task-specific text at the beginning of the opening user message, before queued node contents. The last call supplies the text. The system prefix and its fingerprint depend only on `context` calls.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.subject_message` has no structural obligation, so it needs no implementation root. Each clause states observable behavior.

- "`message` sets the task-specific text at the beginning of the opening user message, before queued node contents." This fixes where the text appears in the produced message. It names no library, type, signature, field or delegation. An implementation could assemble the message in any way that puts the text first, and the text would still be satisfied.
- "The last call supplies the text." This is last-call-wins behavior. A stored field, a fold over calls or any other mechanism gives the same result, so the choice of mechanism is discretionary.
- "The system prefix and its fingerprint depend only on `context` calls." This says the output prefix and its fingerprint are unchanged by `message`. An implementation could compute them in any structure, as long as the results are independent of `message`. This is an input-output property that tests can check.

The requirement has no implementation edges and the review roots are empty. That is consistent with the text, since it prescribes no structure.

behavioral: The three marked tests together cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.subject_message`. I judged them from the supplied test text only and did not read any implementation source.

1. **The message is at the beginning of the opening user message, before queued node contents.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_late_task_message_precedes_the_first_source_in_the_provider_request]` sends a real provider request. It asserts that the user message `starts_with("new task")` and that it contains the source snapshot. The snapshot is therefore after the task text. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_the_item_and_citations]` also checks that the user content starts with the subject heading. It checks that the source text and requirement text appear after the end of the task portion.

2. **The last call supplies the text.** The configured test calls `.message("old task")`, then `contents_of_current_node()`, then `.message("new task")`. It asserts the user message starts with "new task" and does not contain "old task". `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[task_messages_share_a_prefix_and_can_queue_another_node]` sets "superseded" and then a later message after queuing a node. It asserts the agent received exactly `["assess", "verify"]`.

3. **The system prefix and its fingerprint depend only on `context` calls.** In `task_messages_share_a_prefix_and_can_queue_another_node`, each request has prefix "shared" and fingerprint `context_fingerprint("shared")`. This holds while the message values differ ("superseded", "assess", "verify"). Message text therefore does not enter the prefix or the fingerprint.

I found no obligation without a test and no assertion that contradicts the requirement.
